newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher on government loan plan.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher on government loan plan.

text.p: Taiwan shares prices finished higher on Thursday, reflecting investor bullishness following a government announcement to appropriate low-interest loans to first-time homebuyers, brokers said.
The benchmark index ended up 60.38 points or 0.75 percent at 8,089.71. Turnover was a brisk T$130.796 billion.
Taiwan's Interior Ministry said on Thursday it was arranging T$61.47 billion in credits for first-time homebuyers.
"Such news surely helped boost sentiment, but constructions which should be benefited most, did not rise so much after its recent rallies," said Jardine Fleming manager George Hou.
The construction sector rose only 0.34 percent.
The most heavily weighted financials rose 0.83 percent as the loan plan should provide new business for banks and the government-backed loans are low risk, Hou said.
Electronics, which had closed more than three percent up on Wednesday, rose another 1.78 percent.

Notebook computer maker Compal Electronics surged T$5 to T$95.5 and scanner maker Umax Data Systems jumped T$11 T$211 on expectations of sound sales and profit performance starting from the second quarter, brokers said.
